## Who

I'm **Bruno Seznec**, an independent consultant working at CDO/CTO level on
data and AI architecture — knowledge graphs, data governance, and the
increasingly load-bearing junction between the two and LLM systems. I also
train teams on the semantic web stack.

- LinkedIn: [brunoseznec](https://www.linkedin.com/in/brunoseznec/)

## How to reuse this

The notes are published under
[CC BY 4.0](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/) — reuse them freely
with attribution. The slides and abstracts they link to belong to their
respective speakers and are **not** covered by that licence.

## Structured data

Every talk page embeds a `schema.org` JSON-LD block in a `<script>` tag,
describing the talk as an `Event` (linked to the conference via `superEvent`),
the speaker as a `Person`, and the notes themselves as a `BlogPosting` whose
`about` points at the talk.

You can pull the structured data out of any page with an extractor of your
choice, or inspect it in the page source. If you spot a modelling mistake,
[open an issue](https://github.com/brunosez/semantics-2026-notes/issues) — I'd
rather be corrected than consistent.

## Corrections

If I've misrepresented your talk, tell me and I'll fix it. The repository
history is public, so corrections are visible rather than silent.
